observations.trace: The selected YAML loader calls serde_saphyr::from_str for TacticalCombatConfig then validate. Pinned concrete f32 parser handles explicit .nan/.inf; AiOffenseConfig::has_valid_intervals omits hit_precision and the parent checks unrelated targeting.reported_hit_precision. ReportedPrecision::new rejects nonfinite but accepts every finite value, and selected melee/ranged publication calls expect.
observations.remaining: This reconnects original059 Adler and Segovb findings without deciding their global alias. Source reasoning assumes all other startup gates succeed and the AI reaches the relevant branch; no live config, parser, panic, game or product ran.

observations.trace: The same original Adler offense admission record already covers unchecked ranged_standoff_slop_metres. Under a hypothetical otherwise admitted config with slop -1m, weapon reach10m, reach fraction0.5, min1.5m, max12m and target distance5m, standoff is5m but first comparison 5 > 5 - 1 selects forward movement instead of the hold/fire branch.
observations.remaining: Source arithmetic only; no actual ranged weapon, command, accepted config or runtime scene was observed. Positive slop, target and attack identity policies remain open.

observations.trace: The selected validated probability1 can choose the anticipatory fixture branch; non-certain successful rolls sample the authored interval. A single PendingBotReaction component retains only one timer/choice and later insert replaces the previous same-type component.
observations.remaining: Separate conditional policy questions; no random draw, multiple attacks, timing or defense ran.

observations.trace: Validated config digest hashes serde_json bytes, and the selected pinned serializer renders NaN and infinity as null for f32. Given otherwise identical admitted configs differing only by these nonfinite values, their JSON bytes and digests are identical. Startup logs the digest.
observations.remaining: No serialization, hash computation or log was produced. Other digest consumers and intended equality policy remain open.

conditional_findings.first_contract: Dodge probability and anticipatory reaction timing need an explicit independent behavior contract when ordinary configuration can choose certainty.
conditional_findings.source_witness: The ordinary config validator accepts dodge_chance1.0, standard_combat copies it into DefenseChances, and successful reaction scheduling uses an anticipatory (windup - 0.16).clamp(0.02,0.12) whenever chance >=1.0 instead of the configured reaction-delay range. The source comment describes this as an authored test dodger, but the same branch is reachable from ordinary config. The seeded unit_f64 helper is documented as half-open [0,1).
conditional_findings.counterevidence: An always-dodge test fixture intentionally uses this branch. Whether ordinary certain-dodge tuning should also be anticipatory is a design policy, not established by source. A valid1.0 configuration, a given attack, timer event or player outcome was not run.
conditional_findings.effect_and_limits: Assuming an eligible target, 0.65-second windup and otherwise canonical source defaults, a 1.0 chance selects 0.12 seconds, while a 0.999 chance on a successful roll selects the configured 0.20–0.27-second interval. This compares source branches, not an observed random draw, exact floating output or completed dodge.
conditional_findings.repair_direction: When authorized, make ordinary reaction timing and intentionally anticipatory test/fixture behavior independently owned or document the intended coupling, preserving legitimate zero/one probabilities.
conditional_findings.alias_qualification: Recovered059 explicitly noted this anticipatory branch without asserting its ordinary-config route. Global alias and historical unique counts remain open; no checkpoint3821 promotion.

conditional_findings.first_contract: The owner of simultaneous or successive incoming attacks must decide whether a single pending bot reaction can replace an earlier unfinished one.
conditional_findings.source_witness: try_start_reaction queues insert(PendingBotReaction { timer, choice }) on the defender for every successful eligible reaction; the component contains one timer and choice, not the incoming attack identity. The pinned Bevy EntityCommands::insert source states existing same-type components are overwritten. tick_bot_reactions emits and removes the retained reaction when its timer finishes.
conditional_findings.counterevidence: The policy may deliberately choose the latest defense, and a single dodge may address multiple attacks. Source does not establish concurrent requests, scheduling order, target lifecycle, a missed defense or player incident. No event, timer, simulation or runtime was executed.
conditional_findings.effect_and_limits: If a second successful reaction is applied to the same defender before the first timer finishes, its timer and choice replace the earlier component; a later expiration can defer the first pending decision. This is a conditional component-state trace, not proof of duplicate delivery or missed combat performance.
conditional_findings.repair_direction: When authorized, decide and encode the intended priority/coalescing or attack-specific response policy; preserve legitimate defense cancellation for incapacitated actors.
conditional_findings.alias_qualification: Recovered059 separately observed replacement as an unresolved source policy; this explicit conditional scheduling question does not change original status, imply global aliases or recover3821.

conditional_findings.first_contract: A diagnostic digest of an admitted combat configuration should distinguish materially different stored input values, or the admission owner should exclude values that cannot be represented in the digest format.
conditional_findings.source_witness: AiOffenseConfig.hit_precision is raw f32 and the parent validation omits it. Pinned serde-saphyr accepts .nan and +.inf for concrete f32; selected startup calls validation, installs the config and obtains digest through serde_json::to_vec. Pinned serde_json serializes nonfinite f32 values as JSON null. Identical otherwise-valid configs with only this field set to NaN versus positive infinity therefore serialize the same null at that field and hash identical bytes, assuming serialization succeeds.
conditional_findings.counterevidence: This depends on all other fields validating, successful parsing, unpoisoned snapshot lock and successful serialization. Both nonfinite inputs are outside the finite ReportedPrecision consumer contract. The observed digest use is startup logging; no client synchronization gate, actual files, hash value or operational incident was observed.
conditional_findings.effect_and_limits: A source-only conditional diagnostic-identity collapse on distinct admitted numeric values, connected to but downstream from the original precision admission finding. This is not a cryptographic collision claim and no serializer or hash ran.
conditional_findings.repair_direction: When authorized, enforce the selected finite precision admission or otherwise give the digest a representation that faithfully owns every admitted value; preserve legitimate finite negative and >1 precision.
conditional_findings.alias_qualification: Original Adler broad configuration and Segovb specific precision findings keep their separate original attribution and open alias question. This digest consumer is distinct; no accepted historical count or checkpoint3821 recovery is inferred.
